string.text: US Army 5.56 Suppressor

%c[ui_gray_2]COMPATIBILITY:
 
%c[d_cyan] • %c[ui_gray_2] 5.56x45 caliber
 
%c[ui_gray_1]An advanced suppressor for small-caliber rifles, manufactured in the USA. A large number of these for unknown reasons "disappeared" from US Army supply containers. The suppressor consists of a high-strength steel housing with four expansion chambers, followed by a series of Z-type titanium baffles. Effectively reduces muzzle flash and gunshot noise. Requires minimal maintenance. Suppressors of this type are widely used on NATO small-caliber rifles.
 
%c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] Sound suppression: %c[ui_gray_1]medium
9mm Suppressor

%c[ui_gray_2]COMPATIBILITY:
 
%c[d_cyan] • %c[ui_gray_2] 9mm caliber
 
%c[ui_gray_1]A suppressor for 9mm caliber firearms. Archaic in design, yet quite effective. It contains a tightly packed roll of brass mesh inside. The front section of the device houses a set of rubber wipes with apertures for bullet passage. The suppressor is used in close-quarters combat against light-armored targets and for stealth takedowns.

The L26 model, patented in Germany under the name System Schaetzle, differs from similar Russian suppressors based on wipe technology. The L26 utilizes a stack of six identical cone-shaped metal baffles inside a simple tube. It attaches to the rifle via a clamp around the front sight base, precisely like the rifle grenade launcher designed for the K98k.\n \n The basic design was utilized across several models; primarily for any Wehrmacht issue arm in 8mm caliber (excluding the anti-tank rifle...). It was also produced for the MG42, with approximately 200 units fielded for service alongside the MG42.
The KIBA Arms suppressor was developed specifically for installation on 9.3x64mm rifles to effectively suppress heavy magnum charges.
